title: A2B Sells Majority Stake to James Murdoch-Backed Bodhi Tree in $180 Million Deal
excerpt: The Chennai vegetarian chain, valued at about $350 million, will use the investment to expand in western India and Europe and modernise its kitchens. Uday Shankar will chair the new board.
body:
• Adyar Ananda Bhavan (A2B) has sold a majority stake to Bodhi Tree Systems for $180 million (over Rs 1,600 crore), in a transaction valuing the company at approximately $350 million.
  • Bodhi Tree is the investment platform co-founded by James Murdoch and former Star India chief Uday Shankar, who will serve as chairperson of A2B's new board.
  • The money will fund expansion into western India and Europe, modernisation of manufacturing facilities, and growth of A2B's retail and export operations.
  • A2B runs about 160 outlets in India and more than 30 overseas, and reported revenue of about Rs 1,487 crore and net profit of about Rs 36.2 crore for the year ended March 2025.

One of South India's best-known vegetarian restaurant chains has a new controlling owner. Adyar Ananda Bhavan, known everywhere as A2B, has sold a majority stake to Bodhi Tree Systems in a $180 million transaction, the companies said, valuing the Chennai-based business at approximately $350 million.

Bodhi Tree is the investment platform co-founded by James Murdoch, through Lupa Systems, and Uday Shankar, the former Star India chief. Shankar will serve as chairperson of A2B's new board of directors, and Veda Corporate Advisers acted as exclusive financial adviser to A2B on the deal, Storyboard18 reported. The exact percentage acquired was not disclosed.

What the buyer is paying for

A2B was founded in the late 1970s by brothers K. T. Srinivasa Raja and K. T. Venkatesan and has been promoter-led for nearly five decades. It operates about 160 outlets in India, concentrated in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, and more than 30 outlets internationally — in markets including Singapore, the United States, Australia, Malaysia and the United Kingdom — employing over 15,000 staff across restaurants, sweets and packaged foods, Restaurant India reported.

The reported financials behind the valuation: revenue of approximately Rs 1,487 crore and net profit of about Rs 36.2 crore for the financial year ended March 2025.

Where the money goes

Vishnu Shankar, a member of the A2B promoter family, confirmed the transaction to The Hindu and said the investment would fund expansion into new markets in India and overseas, including western India and Europe. The partnership's stated agenda is to strengthen leadership and talent, build digital capabilities, modernise kitchens and manufacturing facilities to global standards, and expand the range of healthy and nutritious food, alongside growing the retail and export operations, afaqs! reported.

Bodhi Tree's third big bet

For Bodhi Tree, A2B is its third major investment, after ALLEN Career Institute and JioStar (including its earlier Rs 13,500 crore investment in Viacom18). The move takes the platform out of media and education and into consumer food — a bet that a regional, family-run food brand can be professionalised and scaled internationally the way its media assets were.

The test will be execution in unfamiliar markets. A2B's strength is a dense, loyal base in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka built on sweets, savouries and casual dining; western India and Europe are markets where that brand recognition has to be built, not inherited.
